The community has 9 proposed rules for how the lake gets fished going forward. Vote for the one you'd rather live under.

1. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 1.2 kg per trip or no more than 10% of the lake’s current biomass, whichever is smaller, while the lake must always retain at least 60% of its total biomass as a communal reserve after the catch.
   In practice: Before each trip a fisher calculates 10% of the lake’s current biomass; if 1.2 kg would exceed that percentage, the fisher may only take the smaller amount. The fisher records the catch in a communal ledger. At the end of each month the council reviews the ledger; if a fisher’s total catch that month exceeds the 10%-based limit, the excess is added to the communal reserve and the fisher receives a one-trip fishing ban. If the lake’s biomass ever falls below the 60% reserve target, all fishers must stop fishing until the reserve is restored. The council meets quarterly to adjust the reserve target if needed.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 0.8 kg per trip, with a cumulative monthly limit of 2 kg; the lake must retain a protected reserve of 40% of its current biomass; the community’s total monthly catch may not exceed 8 kg.
   In practice: Every fishing day, each fisher records the weight taken on a shared log. At the end of each month, the community gathers to audit logs, calculate the lake’s remaining biomass, and verify the protected reserve. If a fisher exceeds 0.8 kg per trip or 2 kg monthly, they forfeit that day’s license for the following month. If the lake’s reserve falls below 40%, all fishing ceases until the reserve reaches the threshold, after which catch limits reset. Monthly adjustments to limits are made if the reserve rises above 45% or if community needs rise, following a simple majority vote.

3. Policy: Fishing is allowed only when the lake holds at least 12 kg and the communal reserve holds at least 12 kg. In that case each fisher may take up to 1.0 kg, keep 1.0 kg for sustenance, and deposit 0.5 kg into the reserve. If the lake falls to 8–12 kg, limits drop to 0.8 kg with a 0.3 kg deposit; if 6–8 kg, limits are 0.5 kg with a 0.2 kg deposit; fishing stops below 6 kg until both lake and reserve reach 12 kg.
   In practice: Before each trip a fisher reads the lake and reserve levels. They record the weight taken and the deposit in a shared ledger after returning. The reserve is updated by adding all deposits. If the reserve falls below 12 kg, no one may fish until it is replenished. A fisher who fishes beyond the limit must return the excess and add an extra 0.1 kg to the reserve as a penalty. The community treasurer checks the ledger each evening and updates the reserve. Anyone who fails to deposit is barred from fishing until the deposit is made.

4. Policy: Fishing may only occur when lake biomass is at least 12 kg; each fisher can take no more than 2 kg per cycle, 1 kg subsistence guaranteed, the other 1 kg optional and subject to a combined 5 % of current biomass; 15 % of the lake must remain permanently reserved.
   In practice: At the start of each six‑month cycle, community leaders measure lake biomass. Fisheries are registered only if the threshold is met. Each fisher logs a 1 kg subsistence catch and may claim up to an additional 1 kg provided total community catch does not exceed 5 % of current biomass. Excess over quota must be returned to the lake. Violations trigger a communal penalty and temporary ban. The 15 % reserve is maintained by ensuring the combined catch never reduces biomass below 15 % of its current level.

5. Policy: Solo may harvest up to 60% of the lake’s current stock per trip, capped at 12 kg; all other fishers may harvest up to 30% of the current stock per trip, capped at 6 kg.
   In practice: Before each trip, the community confirms the lake’s stock and records each fisher’s quota. Solo is allowed to fish up to 12 kg or 60% of the stock, whichever is lower. All other fishers must stay within their 30%/6 kg limit. If a fisher exceeds their quota, they must return the excess fish to the lake within 24 hours and forfeit their license for the next round. The community will hold a quarterly audit to ensure compliance and adjust limits if stock drops below sustainable thresholds.

6. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 70% of the lake’s current stock per trip, must keep 1 kg for sustenance, and deposit 0.5% of the catch into a communal reserve that must always hold at least 5 kg; if the reserve falls below 5 kg, the fisher who caused the dip must contribute 0.5 kg per trip until the reserve reaches 5 kg.
   In practice: On each trip a fisher first measures the lake stock, then calculates 70% of that number as their maximum allowable catch. They set aside 1 kg for personal use. From the remaining catch they give 0.5% to the communal reserve, updating the reserve balance on a community ledger. If after a trip the reserve balance is below 5 kg, the fisher who caused the dip must, on their next trip, add an extra 0.5 kg of their catch to the reserve until the reserve is back to 5 kg. Failure to deposit or to provide the extra 0.5 kg when required results in a 1 kg penalty that the fisher must pay from their next catch.

7. Policy: Maximum 7 kg per fisher per trip, total 150 kg per day, lake reserve 25 kg, 1 kg fee for missing 1 kg catch.
   In practice: Every fisher logs their catch in a shared ledger overseen by the community chair. Before each trip the current lake level is checked; if it would fall below 25 kg after the trip, fishing is paused until restocking. The total of all fishers’ catches is tallied each day; if it exceeds 150 kg, no more trips are allowed that day. Any fisher who fails to reach a 1 kg minimum must immediately deposit 1 kg into the communal restocking pot. The pot is replenished each season and used to boost the lake’s fish population. Repeat violations trigger a community vote that can suspend the fisher’s rights for a set number of days.

8. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 4 kg per trip, but the lake must always hold at least 10 kg of fish; if a catch would drop the lake below 10 kg the fisher must return enough fish to keep it at 10 kg; if a fisher’s catch is less than 1 kg the fisher must deposit 0.5 kg into the communal reserve.
   In practice: Before each trip a fisher records the current lake stock. They fish, then if their catch would leave the lake under 10 kg they return enough fish to keep it at 10 kg. They add 0.5 kg to the communal reserve if their catch is <1 kg. A daily ledger posted on the dock records lake stock and individual catches. Every Friday a random fisher checks another fisher’s ledger; any violation results in a 0.5 kg penalty deducted from the violator’s personal reserve and a one‑round fishing ban.

9. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 4 kg per trip or 12 % of the lake’s current stock, whichever is lower; the lake must retain at least 25 % of its pre‑fishing stock; any catch below 1 kg triggers a 0.5 kg fee to the communal reserve unless the lake holds fewer than 5 kg.
   In practice: Before each trip the fisher records the lake’s current stock and the catch weight. The fisherman must leave at least 25 % of the pre‑fishing stock. The community leader checks the log against a random sample of the lake’s fish counts after the trip. If a fisher violates the catch cap or retention rule, his catch is confiscated and he forfeits the right to fish for the next round. The 0.5 kg fee from any sub‑1 kg catch is deposited into the communal reserve. All logs are posted on the community board so every fisher can verify compliance.

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class ReserveNorm(Norm):
    type_name = "reserve"

    def _balance_state(self, context):
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        # Initialise balance if not present, using starting_balance_kg if provided
        state.setdefault("balance_kg", self.params.get("starting_balance_kg", 0.0))
        return state

    # The reserve now enforces a minimum absolute kilograms, not a percentage of stock.
    # No automatic top‑up – if the balance falls below the minimum, the next fisher
    # simply forfeits the required 5 % deposit (losing it) until the reserve is restored.
    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
        """Report the current reserve balance for the fisher's notice.
        Mirrors the test expectation of a simple integer‑kg sentence.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0)
        return f"The community reserve currently holds {int(balance)}kg."


    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
        """Fisher is eligible unless stock is low and reserve is insufficient.
        Policy: when lake stock is below 6 kg, fishing is suspended until the
        communal reserve has at least 12 kg.
        """
        if context.stock_before < 6:
            state = self._balance_state(context)
            if state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) < 12.0:
                return False
        return True

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.
        * Existing short‑fall withdrawal logic (for low‑catch trips) is retained unchanged.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        # Standard deposit: 0.5 % of the raw catch
        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005
        # Update reserve balance with the standard deposit
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) + deposit
        note_parts = []
        if deposit > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"You deposited {deposit:.3f}kg into the communal reserve.")
        # If reserve is still below the required minimum, take an extra 0.5 kg from the fisher's keep
        extra_contribution = 0.0
        MIN_RESERVE = 5.0
        if balance < MIN_RESERVE:
            # Determine how much can be taken from the fisher's keep (cannot exceed what they have left after the standard deposit)
            available_for_extra = max(0.0, raw_kg - deposit)
            extra_contribution = min(0.5, available_for_extra)
            balance += extra_contribution
            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the reserve minimum.")
        # Store updated balance
        state["balance_kg"] = balance
        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
            withdraw = min(needed, limit, state["balance_kg"])
            if withdraw > 0:
                kept += withdraw
                state["balance_kg"] -= withdraw
                note_parts.append(f"You withdrew {withdraw:.3f}kg from the reserve.")
        note = " ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept, note=note)

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class CommunityCapNorm(Norm):
    type_name = "community_cap"

    def _limit(self, context):
        pct = self.params.get("cap_pct_of_stock")
        if pct is not None:
            return pct * context.stock_before
        if "cap_kg" in self.params:
            return self.params.get("cap_kg")
        # No cap configured – treat as unlimited (no-op)
        return None

    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
        limit = self._limit(context)
        if limit is None:
            return None
        used = context.round_scratch(self.key).get("total_kg", 0.0)
        return f"The community has {max(0.0, limit - used):.0f}kg left of its shared allowance for this round."

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        limit = self._limit(context)
        if limit is None:
            # No cap – allow all
            return NormDecision.allow(proposed_kg)
        tally = context.round_scratch(self.key)
        used = tally.get("total_kg", 0.0)
        remaining = max(0.0, limit - used)
        if proposed_kg <= remaining:
            tally["total_kg"] = used + proposed_kg
            return NormDecision.allow(proposed_kg)
        # Exceeds remaining allowance
        tally["total_kg"] = used + remaining
        return NormDecision.violation(
            kept_kg=remaining,
            sanction="over_community_cap",
            note="The community's shared allowance for this round was already used up by others, so the rest of your catch wasn't counted.",
        )

        threshold = self.params.get("replenish_if_over_pct")
        if threshold is None:

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class ViolationBanNorm(Norm):
    type_name = "violation_ban"

    def _ban_state(self, context, agent_id):
        return context.norm_state(self.key).setdefault(agent_id, {"trips_remaining": 0})

    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
        ban = self._ban_state(context, agent_id)
        if ban["trips_remaining"] > 0:
            ban["trips_remaining"] -= 1
            return False
        return True

    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
        remaining = self._ban_state(context, agent_id)["trips_remaining"]
        if remaining > 0:

# Skill: understand

# /understand

Analyze the current codebase and produce a `knowledge-graph.json` file in the project's data directory (`.ua/`, or the legacy `.understand-anything/` when it already exists). This file powers the interactive dashboard for exploring the project's architecture.

## Options

- `$ARGUMENTS` may contain:
  - `--full` — Force a full rebuild, ignoring any existing graph
  - `--auto-update` — Enable automatic graph updates on commit (writes `autoUpdate: true` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--no-auto-update` — Disable automatic graph updates (writes `autoUpdate: false` to `$UA_DIR/config.json`)
  - `--review` — Run full LLM graph-reviewer instead of inline deterministic validation
  - `--language <lang>` — Generate all textual content (summaries, descriptions, tags, titles, languageNotes, languageLesson) in the specified language. Accepts ISO 639-1 codes (`zh`, `ja`, `ko`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `de`, etc.) or friendly names (`chinese`, `japanese`, `korean`, `english`, `spanish`, etc.). Locale variants supported: `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, etc. Defaults to `en` (English). Stores preference in `$UA_DIR/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates.
  - `--exclude <patterns>` — Comma-separated glob patterns for additional files/directories to exclude from analysis (e.g., `--exclude "tests/*,docs/*"`). These patterns take highest priority over built-in defaults and `.understandignore` rules. Supports gitignore syntax including `!` negation.
  - A directory path (e.g. `/path/to/repo` or `../other-project`) — Analyze the given directory instead of the current working directory

---

## Progress Reporting

Throughout execution, report progress to the user at each phase transition and during batch processing. This keeps users informed on large codebases where analysis can take a long time.

- **Phase transitions:** At the start of each phase, print a status line:
  > `[Phase N/7] <phase name>...`
  >
  > Example: `[Phase 2/7] Analyzing files (12 batches)...`

- **Batch progress:** During Phase 2, report each batch with its index and total:
  > `Analyzing batch X/N (files: foo.ts, bar.ts, ...)` (list up to 3 filenames, then `...` if more)

- **Phase completion:** When a phase finishes, briefly confirm:
  > `Phase N complete. <one-line summary of result>`
  >
  > Example: `Phase 1 complete. Found 247 files across 3 languages.`

     - Verify the resolved path exists and is a directory (run `test -d <path>`). If it does not exist or is not a directory, report an error to the user and **STOP**.

Detect a worktree by comparing `git rev-parse --git-dir` against `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`; in a normal checkout or submodule they resolve to the same path, in a worktree they differ and the parent of `--git-common-dir` is the main repo root.

     ```bash
     COMMON_DIR=$(git -C "$PROJECT_ROOT" rev-parse --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null)

       GIT_ABS=$(cd "$PROJECT_ROOT" && cd "$GIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
       if [ -n "$COMMON_ABS" ] && [ "$COMMON_ABS" != "$GIT_ABS" ]; then
         MAIN_ROOT=$(dirname "$COMMON_ABS")
         if [ -d "$MAIN_ROOT" ] && [ "${UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT:-0}" != "1" ]; then
           echo "[understand] Detected git worktree at $PROJECT_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] Redirecting output to main repo root: $MAIN_ROOT"
           echo "[understand] (Set UNDERSTAND_NO_WORKTREE_REDIRECT=1 to keep PROJECT_ROOT as the worktree.)"
           PROJECT_ROOT="$MAIN_ROOT"
         fi

#### Default path (no `--review`): inline deterministic validation

Write the following Node.js script to `$UA_DIR/tmp/ua-inline-validate.cjs`:

```javascript
#!/usr/bin/env node
const fs = require('fs');
const graphPath = process.argv[2];
const outputPath = process.argv[3];
try {
  const graph = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(graphPath, 'utf8'));
  const issues = [], warnings = [];
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.nodes)) { issues.push('graph.nodes is missing or not an array'); graph.nodes = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.edges)) { issues.push('graph.edges is missing or not an array'); graph.edges = []; }
  const nodeIds = new Set();
  const seen = new Map();
  graph.nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    if (!n.id) { issues.push(`Node[${i}] missing id`); return; }
    if (!n.type) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing type`);
    if (!n.name) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing name`);
    if (!n.summary) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing summary`);
    if (!n.tags || !n.tags.length) issues.push(`Node[${i}] '${n.id}' missing tags`);
    if (seen.has(n.id)) issues.push(`Duplicate node ID '${n.id}' at indices ${seen.get(n.id)} and ${i}`);
    else seen.set(n.id, i);
    nodeIds.add(n.id);
  });
  graph.edges.forEach((e, i) => {
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.source)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] source '${e.source}' not found`);
    if (!nodeIds.has(e.target)) issues.push(`Edge[${i}] target '${e.target}' not found`);
  });
  const fileLevelTypes = new Set(['file', 'config', 'document', 'service', 'pipeline', 'table', 'schema', 'resource', 'endpoint']);
  const fileNodes = graph.nodes.filter(n => fileLevelTypes.has(n.type)).map(n => n.id);
  const assigned = new Map();
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.layers)) { if (graph.layers) warnings.push('graph.layers is not an array'); graph.layers = []; }
  if (!Array.isArray(graph.tour)) { if (graph.tour) warnings.push('graph.tour is not an array'); graph.tour = []; }
  graph.layers.forEach(layer => {
    (layer.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Layer '${layer.id}' refs missing node '${id}'`);
      if (assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`Node '${id}' appears in multiple layers`);
      assigned.set(id, layer.id);
    });
  });
  fileNodes.forEach(id => {
    if (!assigned.has(id)) issues.push(`File node '${id}' not in any layer`);
  });
  graph.tour.forEach((step, i) => {
    (step.nodeIds || []).forEach(id => {
      if (!nodeIds.has(id)) issues.push(`Tour step[${i}] refs missing node '${id}'`);
    });
  });
  const withEdges = new Set([
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.source),
    ...graph.edges.map(e => e.target)
  ]);
  graph.nodes.forEach(n => {
    if (!withEdges.has(n.id)) warnings.push(`Node '${n.id}' has no edges (orphan)`);
  });
  const stats = {
    totalNodes: graph.nodes.length,
    totalEdges: graph.edges.length,
    totalLayers: graph.layers.length,
    tourSteps: graph.tour.length,
    nodeTypes: graph.nodes.reduce((a, n) => { a[n.type] = (a[n.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {}),
    edgeTypes: graph.edges.reduce((a, e) => { a[e.type] = (a[e.type]||0)+1; return a; }, {})
  };
  fs.writeFileSync(outputPath, JSON.stringify({ issues, warnings, stats }, null, 2));
  process.exit(0);
} catch (err) { process.stderr.write(err.message + '\n'); process.exit(1); }
```

19	# whatever's been trimmed off by every norm that already ran this call. If

22	# nothing rather than raising an error, so get the order right.
23	
24	from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision
25	
26	
27	class ReserveNorm(Norm):
28	    type_name = "reserve"
29	
30	    def _balance_state(self, context):
31	        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
32	        # Initialise balance if not present, using starting_balance_kg if provided
33	        state.setdefault("balance_kg", self.params.get("starting_balance_kg", 0.0))
34	        return state
35	
36	    # The reserve now enforces a minimum absolute kilograms, not a percentage of stock.
37	    # No automatic top‑up – if the balance falls below the minimum, the next fisher
38	    # simply forfeits the required 5 % deposit (losing it) until the reserve is restored.
39	    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
40	        """Report the current reserve balance for the fisher's notice.
41	        Mirrors the test expectation of a simple integer‑kg sentence.
42	        """
43	        state = self._balance_state(context)
44	        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0)
45	        return f"The community reserve currently holds {int(balance)}kg."
46	
47	
48	    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
49	        """Fisher is eligible unless stock is low and reserve is insufficient.
50	        Policy: when lake stock is below 6 kg, fishing is suspended until the
51	        communal reserve has at least 12 kg.
52	        """
53	        if context.stock_before < 6:
54	            state = self._balance_state(context)
55	            if state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) < 12.0:
56	                return False
57	        return True
58	
59	    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
60	        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
61	        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
62	        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
63	        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.
64	        * Existing short‑fall withdrawal logic (for low‑catch trips) is retained unchanged.
65	        """
66	        state = self._balance_state(context)
67	        # Standard deposit: 0.5 % of the raw catch
68	        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005
69	        # Update reserve balance with the standard deposit
70	        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) + deposit
71	        note_parts = []
72	        if deposit > 0:
73	            note_parts.append(f"You deposited {deposit:.3f}kg into the communal reserve.")
74	        # Ensure reserve stays at least 15 % of lake stock after deposit
75	        MIN_RESERVE = 0.15 * context.stock_before
76	        if balance < MIN_RESERVE:
77	            # Take extra from fisher's keep to meet minimum reserve
78	            needed = MIN_RESERVE - balance
79	            # Cannot take more than what fisher has left after deposit
80	            available = max(0.0, raw_kg - deposit)
81	            extra_contribution = min(needed, available)
82	            balance += extra_contribution
83	            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the reserve minimum.")
84	        # Store updated balance
85	        state["balance_kg"] = balance
86	        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
87	        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
88	        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
89	        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
90	        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
91	        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
92	            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
93	            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
94	            withdraw = min(needed, limit, state["balance_kg"])
95	            if withdraw > 0:
96	                kept += withdraw
97	                state["balance_kg"] -= withdraw
98	                note_parts.append(f"You withdrew {withdraw:.3f}kg from the reserve.")
99	        note = " ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
100	        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept, note=note)

41	        Mirrors the test expectation of a simple integer‑kg sentence.

45	        return f"The community reserve currently holds {int(balance)}kg."
46

49	        """Fisher is eligible unless stock is low and reserve is insufficient.
50	        Policy: when lake stock is below 6 kg, fishing is suspended until the
51	        communal reserve has at least 12 kg.
52	        """
53	        if context.stock_before < 6:
54	            state = self._balance_state(context)
55	            if state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) < 12.0:
56	                return False
57	        return True
58	
59	    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
60	        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
61	        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
62	        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
63	        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.

68	        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005

71	        note_parts = []
72	        if deposit > 0:

74	        # Ensure reserve stays at least 15 % of lake stock after deposit
75	        MIN_RESERVE = 0.15 * context.stock_before
76	        if balance < MIN_RESERVE:
77	            # Take extra from fisher's keep to meet minimum reserve
78	            needed = MIN_RESERVE - balance
79	            # Cannot take more than what fisher has left after deposit
80	            available = max(0.0, raw_kg - deposit)
81	            extra_contribution = min(needed, available)
82	            balance += extra_contribution
83	            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the reserve minimum.")
84	        # Store updated balance
85	        state["balance_kg"] = balance
86	        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
87	        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
88	        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
89	        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
90	        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
91	        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
92	            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
93	            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
94	            withdraw = min(needed, limit, state["balance_kg"])
95	            if withdraw > 0:
96	                kept += withdraw
97	                state["balance_kg"] -= withdraw

        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.

        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.

        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.

from norms.reserve import ReserveNorm


def _context(runtime=None):
    return HarvestContext.from_state({
        "config": {}, "fluents": [], "runtime": runtime or {"stock_kg": 100.0},
        "agents": {}, "round_number": 1,
    })


def test_deposits_the_trimmed_excess():
    norm = ReserveNorm(key="reserve", params={})
    context = _context()
    # raw_kg=15, proposed_kg=10 -> an earlier cap norm already trimmed 5kg
    decision = norm.evaluate(context, "agent_0", raw_kg=15.0, proposed_kg=10.0)
    # Deposit 0.5% of raw (0.075kg) + extra 0.5kg to meet reserve minimum
    assert decision.kept_kg == 15.0 - 0.075 - 0.5
    assert abs(context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] - (0.075 + 0.5)) < 1e-6


def test_no_excess_when_nothing_was_trimmed():
    norm = ReserveNorm(key="reserve", params={})
    context = _context()
    norm.evaluate(context, "agent_0", raw_kg=10.0, proposed_kg=10.0)
    # Deposit 0.5% of raw (0.05kg) + extra 0.5kg
    assert abs(context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] - (0.05 + 0.5)) < 1e-6
    # Kept kg should reflect deposit and extra contribution
    # (not asserted here as decision not captured)


def test_withdrawal_capped_by_max_withdrawal_kg():
    norm = ReserveNorm(key="reserve", params={"shortfall_threshold_kg": 20, "max_withdrawal_kg": 2})
    context = _context()
    context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] = 100.0
    decision = norm.evaluate(context, "agent_0", raw_kg=1.0, proposed_kg=1.0)
    # Deposit 0.005kg, extra 0.5kg, then withdraw up to available balance (0.505kg) limited by max_withdrawal 2kg
    # After withdrawal, kept should be 1.0 (original) - deposit - extra + withdrawn = 1.0
    assert abs(decision.kept_kg - 1.0) < 1e-6
    # Balance should be 0 after withdrawing the 0.505kg added earlier
    assert abs(context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"]) < 1e-6


def test_no_withdrawal_when_above_threshold():
    norm = ReserveNorm(key="reserve", params={"shortfall_threshold_kg": 5})
    context = _context()
    context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] = 50.0
    decision = norm.evaluate(context, "agent_0", raw_kg=10.0, proposed_kg=10.0)
    # Deposit 0.05kg, extra 0.5kg, no withdrawal because kept (9.45kg) > threshold
    assert abs(decision.kept_kg - (10.0 - 0.05 - 0.5)) < 1e-6

def test_starting_balance_only_applies_once():
    norm = ReserveNorm(key="reserve", params={"starting_balance_kg": 10.0})
    context = _context()
    norm.evaluate(context, "agent_0", raw_kg=10.0, proposed_kg=10.0)  # no excess, first touch
    # Balance should be starting + deposit + extra
    expected_balance = 10.0 + 0.05 + 0.5
    assert abs(context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] - expected_balance) < 1e-6

    # Simulate a later round reusing the same persisted runtime state: a
    # fresh Norm instance (as load_norms() creates every round) must not
    # re-apply starting_balance_kg on top of what's already accumulated.
    context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] = 2.0
    fresh_norm = ReserveNorm(key="reserve", params={"starting_balance_kg": 10.0})
    fresh_norm.evaluate(context, "agent_0", raw_kg=10.0, proposed_kg=10.0)
    assert context.norm_state("reserve")["balance_kg"] == 2.0

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class ReserveNorm(Norm):
    type_name = "reserve"

    def _balance_state(self, context):
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        # Initialise balance if not present, using starting_balance_kg if provided
        state.setdefault("balance_kg", self.params.get("starting_balance_kg", 0.0))
        return state

    # The reserve now enforces a minimum absolute kilograms, not a percentage of stock.
    # No automatic top‑up – if the balance falls below the minimum, the next fisher
    # simply forfeits the required 5 % deposit (losing it) until the reserve is restored.
    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
        """Report the current reserve balance for the fisher's notice.
        Mirrors the test expectation of a simple integer‑kg sentence.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0)
        return f"The community reserve currently holds {int(balance)}kg."


    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
        """Fisher is eligible unless stock is low and reserve is insufficient.
        Policy: when lake stock is below 6 kg, fishing is suspended until the
        communal reserve has at least 12 kg.
        """
        if context.stock_before < 6:
            state = self._balance_state(context)
            if state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) < 12.0:
                return False
        return True

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.
        * Existing short‑fall withdrawal logic (for low‑catch trips) is retained unchanged.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        # Deposit 0.5 % of the raw catch
        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005
        # Update reserve balance with the standard deposit
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) + deposit
        note_parts = []
        if deposit > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"You deposited {deposit:.3f}kg into the communal reserve.")
        # Always add a fixed extra contribution of up to 0.5 kg from the fisher's keep
        # (cannot exceed what the fisher has left after the deposit)
        extra_contribution = min(0.5, max(0.0, raw_kg - deposit))
        if extra_contribution > 0:
            balance += extra_contribution
            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the reserve minimum.")
        # Store updated balance
        state["balance_kg"] = balance
        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
            # The amount that can be returned is at most what was taken from the fisher
            max_possible_return = deposit + extra_contribution
            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
            withdraw = min(needed, limit, max_possible_return)
            if withdraw > 0:
                kept += withdraw
                # All of the reserve added this round is returned, resetting balance to 0
                state["balance_kg"] = 0
                note_parts.append(f"You withdrew {withdraw:.3f}kg from the reserve.")
        note = " ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept, note=note)

1	# violation_ban — a multi-trip fishing ban for whoever the round's fully-
2	# chained NormDecision reports a matching sanction for. Persistent per-agent
3	# countdown at context.norm_state(key)[agent_id]["trips_remaining"].
4	#
5	# Config:
6	#     {
7	#       "type": "violation_ban",
8	#       "id": "violation_ban",
9	#       "trigger_sanction": "over_cap",  # which NormDecision.sanction starts a ban
10	#       "trips": 2                       # ban length, in rounds skipped
11	#     }
12	#
13	# The countdown decrements lazily, inside is_eligible() itself, exactly once
14	# per round (that method is called at most once per agent per round, from
15	# phases/harvest.py's run() loop) — this is what makes "trips": 2 mean
16	# "skipped for exactly 2 rounds", not 1: the round a violation happens the
17	# agent has already fished (the ban starts next round), and the ban ends the
18	# round after trips_remaining ticks down to 0.
19	
20	from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision
21	
22	
23	class ViolationBanNorm(Norm):
24	    type_name = "violation_ban"
25	
26	    def _ban_state(self, context, agent_id):
27	        return context.norm_state(self.key).setdefault(agent_id, {"trips_remaining": 0})
28	
29	    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
30	        ban = self._ban_state(context, agent_id)
31	        if ban["trips_remaining"] > 0:
32	            ban["trips_remaining"] -= 1
33	            return False
34	        return True
35	
36	    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
37	        remaining = self._ban_state(context, agent_id)["trips_remaining"]
38	        if remaining > 0:
39	            return f"You're currently banned from fishing for {remaining} more trip(s)."
40	        return None
41	
42	    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
43	        return NormDecision.allow(proposed_kg)  # a banned agent never reaches evaluate()
44	
45	    def on_agent_settled(self, context, agent_id, decision, harvested_kg):
46	        trigger = self.params.get("trigger_sanction", "deposit_forfeit")
47	        if trigger and decision.sanction == trigger:
48	            self._ban_state(context, agent_id)["trips_remaining"] = self.params.get("trips", 3)

1	# reserve — a shared community reserve, fed by whatever an earlier norm in
2	# config order withheld from an agent this round (deposit), which
3	# low-catchers can draw from to top up a short trip (withdraw). Persistent
4	# balance lives at context.norm_state(key)["balance_kg"].
5	#
6	# Config:
7	#     {
8	#       "type": "reserve",
9	#       "id": "reserve",
10	#       "shortfall_threshold_kg": 5,   # below this kept_kg, eligible to withdraw
11	#       "max_withdrawal_kg": 4,        # per-trip withdrawal ceiling
12	#       "starting_balance_kg": 0       # only read the first round this norm's
13	#                                       # persistent state is empty; never
14	#                                       # resets an existing balance later
15	#     }
16	#
17	# Place this norm *after* any cap-type norm (e.g. catch_limit) in
18	# state["config"]["norms"] — evaluate() deposits raw_kg - proposed_kg, i.e.
19	# whatever's been trimmed off by every norm that already ran this call. If
20	# nothing ran before it, that's 0 and there's nothing to deposit that round
21	# for that agent, which is correct — but a misordering silently deposits
22	# nothing rather than raising an error, so get the order right.
23	
24	from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision
25	
26	
27	class ReserveNorm(Norm):
28	    type_name = "reserve"
29	
30	    def _balance_state(self, context):
31	        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
32	        # Initialise balance if not present, using starting_balance_kg if provided
33	        state.setdefault("balance_kg", self.params.get("starting_balance_kg", 0.0))
34	        return state
35	
36	    # The reserve now enforces a minimum absolute kilograms, not a percentage of stock.
37	    # No automatic top‑up – if the balance falls below the minimum, the next fisher
38	    # simply forfeits the required 5 % deposit (losing it) until the reserve is restored.
39	    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
40	        """Report the current reserve balance for the fisher's notice.
41	        Mirrors the test expectation of a simple integer‑kg sentence.
42	        """
43	        state = self._balance_state(context)
44	        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0)
45	        return f"The community reserve currently holds {int(balance)}kg."
46	
47	
48	    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
49	        """Fisher is eligible unless stock is low and reserve is insufficient.
50	        Policy: when lake stock is below 6 kg, fishing is suspended until the
51	        communal reserve has at least 12 kg.
52	        """
53	        if context.stock_before < 6:
54	            state = self._balance_state(context)
55	            if state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) < 12.0:
56	                return False
57	        return True
58	
59	    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
60	        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
61	        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
62	        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
63	        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.
64	        * Existing short‑fall withdrawal logic (for low‑catch trips) is retained unchanged.
65	        """
66	        state = self._balance_state(context)
67	        # Standard deposit: 0.5 % of the raw catch
68	        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005
69	        # Update reserve balance with the standard deposit
70	        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) + deposit
71	        note_parts = []
72	        if deposit > 0:
73	            note_parts.append(f"You deposited {deposit:.3f}kg into the communal reserve.")
74	        # Ensure reserve stays at least 15 % of lake stock after deposit
75	        MIN_RESERVE = 0.15 * context.stock_before
76	        if balance < MIN_RESERVE:
77	            # Take extra from fisher's keep to meet minimum reserve
78	            needed = MIN_RESERVE - balance
79	            # Cannot take more than what fisher has left after deposit
80	            available = max(0.0, raw_kg - deposit)
81	            extra_contribution = min(needed, available)
82	            balance += extra_contribution
83	            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the reserve minimum.")
84	        # Store updated balance
85	        state["balance_kg"] = balance
86	        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
87	        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
88	        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
89	        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
90	        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
91	        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
92	            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
93	            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
94	            withdraw = min(needed, limit, state["balance_kg"])
95	            if withdraw > 0:
96	                kept += withdraw
97	                state["balance_kg"] -= withdraw
98	                note_parts.append(f"You withdrew {withdraw:.3f}kg from the reserve.")
99	        note = " ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
100	        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept, note=note)

1	# catch_limit — a per-trip kg ceiling, flat or as a percentage of current
2	# stock. Absorbs mechanisms/effort.py's former effort_cap() wholesale (same
3	# per-agent-override behavior), generalized to also support a
4	# percentage-of-stock limit that recomputes every round.
5	#
6	# Config (one entry of state["config"]["norms"]):
7	#     {
8	#       "type": "catch_limit",
9	#       "id": "catch_limit",                   # optional, defaults to "type"
10	#       "limit_kg": 12,                        # flat per-trip ceiling, OR
11	#       "limit_pct_of_stock": 0.1,             # fraction of stock_before, OR
12	#       "limits_by_agent_kg": {"agent_3": 8}   # optional per-agent override,
13	#                                               # takes precedence over either
14	#     }
15	# If both limit_kg and limit_pct_of_stock are set, limit_pct_of_stock wins
16	# (it's always current; limit_kg is not).
17	
18	from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision
19	
20	
21	class CatchLimitNorm(Norm):
22	    type_name = "catch_limit"
23	
24	    def _limit_for(self, context, agent_id):
25	        # Updated policy:
26	        # - Fishing only allowed if lake biomass ≥12 kg.
27	        # - Each fisher may take up to 2 kg per trip.
28	        #   * 1 kg is guaranteed subsistence.
29	        #   * The second kilogram is optional and limited by 5 % of the current stock.
30	        stock = context.stock_before
31	        if stock < 12:
32	            return 0.0
33	        # Optional portion cannot exceed 5 % of stock, capped at 1 kg
34	        optional_limit = min(1.0, 0.05 * stock)
35	        return 1.0 + optional_limit
36	
37	    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
38	        limit = self._limit_for(context, agent_id)
39	        if limit == 0.0:
40	            return None
41	        return f"You currently have an agreed limit of {limit:g}kg for this trip."
42	
43	    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
44	        limit = self._limit_for(context, agent_id)
45	        if limit == 0.0:
46	            # Suspension: fisher keeps nothing but no violation flag
47	            return NormDecision.allow(0.0)
48	        if proposed_kg <= limit:
49	            return NormDecision.allow(proposed_kg)
50	        return NormDecision.violation(
51	            kept_kg=limit,
52	            sanction="over_cap",
53	            note=f"That's more than your {limit:g}kg limit for the trip — the rest wasn't counted.",
54	        )

        """Fisher is eligible unless stock is low and reserve is insufficient.
        Policy: when lake stock is below 6 kg, fishing is suspended until the

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.
        * Existing short‑fall withdrawal logic (for low‑catch trips) is retained unchanged.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        # Standard deposit: 0.5 % of the raw catch
        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005
        # Update reserve balance with the standard deposit
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) + deposit
        note_parts = []
        if deposit > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"You deposited {deposit:.3f}kg into the communal reserve.")
        # Ensure reserve stays at least 70 % of lake biomass after this catch
        # We'll compute needed reserve after we know how much the fisher keeps (tentative).
        # For now, keep the raw catch as tentative kept amount; adjustments will be made later.
        tentative_kept = raw_kg - deposit
        # Minimum required reserve after catch
        min_reserve = 0.7 * (context.stock_before - tentative_kept)
        extra_contribution = 0.0
        if balance < min_reserve:
            needed = min_reserve - balance
            # Fisher can contribute at most what they have left after deposit
            available = max(0.0, tentative_kept)
            extra_contribution = min(needed, available)
            balance += extra_contribution
            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the 70% reserve requirement.")
        # Store updated balance
        state["balance_kg"] = balance
        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
            withdraw = min(needed, limit, state["balance_kg"])
            if withdraw > 0:
                kept += withdraw
                state["balance_kg"] -= withdraw
                note_parts.append(f"You withdrew {withdraw:.3f}kg from the reserve.")
        note = " ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept, note=note)

1. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 1.0 kg per trip or no more than 7 % of the lake’s current biomass, whichever is smaller, and the lake must retain at least 75 % of its total biomass as a communal reserve after each catch.
   In practice: At the start of each trip, a fisher looks at the current lake biomass and calculates the smaller of 1.0 kg or 7 % of that figure; that is the maximum they may take. After their catch, the community ledger records the new lake biomass and the remaining reserve. If a fisher’s catch would drop the reserve below 75 %, they must reduce their haul until the reserve threshold is met. All catches are logged by a designated keeper who meets monthly with the community to audit compliance. Anyone who exceeds the allowed amount must immediately return the excess to the lake in the next trip; repeated violations trigger a temporary fishing ban until the lake biomass recovers to the reserve level.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 1.0 kg per trip, with a cumulative monthly limit of 1.5 kg per fisher; the lake must retain a protected reserve equal to 50 % of its current biomass; the community’s total monthly catch may not exceed 7 kg.
   In practice: At the start of each calendar month the community will measure the lake’s biomass using agreed sampling; 50 % of that value is set aside as protected reserve. Every fisher logs each trip in a shared ledger, noting trip weight and date. If a fisher attempts to take more than 1.0 kg in a single trip, they must stop and return any excess catch to the lake. At month‑end, each fisher’s cumulative catch is summed; if it exceeds 1.5 kg, the excess must be released. The community monitor (rotating monthly) verifies ledger entries and ensures the total community catch does not surpass 7 kg; if it does, the month’s remaining fishing quota is suspended until the next month. Failure to adhere to the per‑trip or monthly limits results in a one‑month suspension of that fisher’s license, and any excess catch must be returned immediately.

3. Policy: Fishing is allowed when the lake holds at least 10 kg and the communal reserve holds at least 8 kg; each fisher may take up to 1 kg per trip, keep 0.6 kg for sustenance, and deposit 0.4 kg into the reserve. When either stock falls below its threshold, fishing stops until both recover.
   In practice: After each trip, the fisher reports catch to the community board and updates the lake and reserve balances. The fisher physically transfers the 0.4 kg deposit to the reserve container. If a fisher exceeds the 1 kg limit or fails to deposit, the board issues a warning; repeated violations result in a one‑month suspension of fishing rights. The community meets monthly to review reserve levels and adjust thresholds if needed.

4. Policy: Fishing may occur only when lake biomass is at least 30 kg; each fisher may harvest up to 3 % of the current lake biomass per six‑month cycle, with 25 % of the biomass permanently reserved; 1 kg of subsistence is included within the 3 % quota and any catch beyond the quota must be returned to the lake.
   In practice: Every first of the month the community council measures lake biomass by a standardized net survey and publishes the result.  Fishers log each catch on a shared ledger; if a fisher’s catch exceeds their 3 % quota, they must return the excess to the lake within 24 hours or face a one‑cycle fishing ban.  Violations are recorded and the council imposes penalties such as community service or temporary suspension.  The permanent 25 % reserve is tracked on the ledger and any attempt to harvest beyond it is prohibited.

5. Policy: Solo may harvest up to 70% of the lake's current stock per trip, capped at 12 kg; all other fishers may harvest up to 30% per trip, capped at 6 kg.
   In practice: At the start of each trip, the lake’s current stock is recorded. Each fisher may take a catch that is no more than the specified percentage of that stock, but not exceeding the cap. After each trip, fishers report their catch to a community ledger. If a fisher exceeds the allowed amount, the excess must be returned to the lake and a fine of one unit of reserve is imposed, or they are barred from the next trip. The rule is reviewed and enforced every 5 trips during a community meeting.

6. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 70% of the lake’s current stock per trip, must keep 1 kg for personal sustenance, and must deposit 0.5% of the remaining catch into a communal reserve that must always hold at least 5 kg. If a fisher’s catch drops the reserve below 5 kg, that fisher must contribute an extra 0.5 kg of catch to the reserve each subsequent trip until the reserve is restored.
   In practice: At the start of a trip, a fisher notes the lake’s current stock (S). They may take up to 0.70·S kg. From that catch they set aside 1 kg for themselves; the remaining catch (C = 0.70·S – 1) is subject to a deposit of 0.5% × C kg into the communal reserve. The reserve pool is tracked each trip. If the deposit would leave the reserve below 5 kg, the fisher who caused the dip must instead deposit 0.5 kg from their catch (in addition to the 0.5% rule) on every following trip until the reserve is back to at least 5 kg. All other fishers follow the same procedure. The lake’s stock is reduced by the amount taken; no further restrictions are applied beyond these steps.

7. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 15 kg per trip; the community’s total daily catch is capped at 250 kg; the lake must retain at least 30 kg of fish at all times; if a fisher fails to catch at least 1 kg they must contribute 1 kg to a communal restocking fund.
   In practice: On each fishing day, all fishers set out together at dawn. Each fisher keeps any fish caught up to the 15 kg limit. The community tracks the total catch; if the 250 kg cap would be exceeded, the remaining quota is divided proportionally among fishers. Any fisher who catches less than 1 kg pays 1 kg from their catch to the restocking fund. The restocking fund is stored as a reserve of fish that may be released if the lake’s fish population drops below 30 kg. If a fisher fails to meet the 1 kg minimum for three consecutive trips, they are suspended from fishing for one week.

8. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 5 kg per trip, but the lake must always hold at least 15 kg of fish; if a fisher’s catch falls below 1 kg, they deposit 0.5 kg into a communal reserve used only when a fisher cannot catch 1 kg.
   In practice: Before each trip, the community checks the lake’s stock with a quick visual count or simple gauge; if it is below 15 kg, no one may fish until the reserve is replenished. Each fisher writes down their catch on a shared ledger. If a fisher’s catch is less than 1 kg, they must add 0.5 kg to the communal reserve; that reserve is tracked and can be drawn from in equal shares when a fisher’s reserves fall below 1 kg. Anyone who fails to deposit gets a 0.5 kg penalty deducted from their next catch.

9. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 4 kg per trip or 10 % of the lake’s current stock, whichever is lower; the lake must retain at least 30 % of its pre‑fishing stock; any catch below 1 kg incurs a 0.5 kg fee to the communal reserve unless the lake holds fewer than 5 kg.
   In practice: Before fishing, each fisher submits a short log of intended catch weight. During the trip, they can only catch within the limit; the catch weight is weighed and recorded by a designated community observer. The observer reports the actual catch to the fisher council each day. If a fisher exceeds the limit, they must pay double the fee (1 kg) to the communal reserve and cannot fish again that week. The communal reserve is monitored monthly; any deficit triggers a temporary rule of 2 kg maximum until the reserve reaches 5 kg. All catch records are kept in a shared ledger visible to all members.

97	def render_survival_status(agent_id, runtime):
98	    """Fishing isn't just for profit — every fisher owes a fixed cost just
99	    to feed themselves each trip, tracked as a running balance that goes
100	    back to round 0, not reset each round. Ties directly to the mechanic in
101	    phases/harvest.py: apply_consumption()/is_dead() decide the same
102	    balance this renders. Deliberately repeated on every phase's prompt,
103	    not just harvest's, matching how Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent restates this
104	    same survival framing in every one of its own prompt templates
105	    (strategy/punishment/norm-update/vote), not only the harvest one."""
106	    balance = runtime.get("payoff", {}).get(agent_id, 0.0)
107	    return (
108	        f"Fishing isn't just for profit — you need roughly {CONSUMPTION_KG:.0f}kg a trip just to "
109	        f"keep yourself fed. Your running reserves stand at {balance:.1f}kg right now; if that "

150	def _harvest_shortfall_clause(mine_record, entry):
151	    """Norm plugins (norms/*.py, orchestrated by engine/norms/engine.py)
152	    enforce themselves by reducing/zeroing an agent's harvested_kg (a cap, a
153	    ban, a reserve draw) — this is what makes sure the affected agent
154	    actually learns that, rather than only ever seeing the resulting kg
155	    number with no way to tell an enforced outcome apart from one they
156	    freely chose. A NormDecision.note (round_record["agents"][agent_id]
157	    ["note"]) is preferred verbatim when a norm authored one — it's the
158	    specific, in-world sentence that norm chose (an over-cap trim, a reserve
159	    top-up). Falls back to a generic derived sentence when no norm bothered
160	    to explain itself: catch_from_effort() is pure and mechanism-agnostic,
161	    so re-running it on the agent's own recorded effort against that
162	    round's starting stock gives what their effort alone would have
163	    produced with nothing else in play. If the agent wasn't even asked that
164	    round (a live ban — norms/violation_ban.py's is_eligible() hook, not
165	    something inferable from numbers alone), "participated": False is set
166	    explicitly by phases/harvest.py; anything else defaults to
167	    participated.
168	    """
169	    if mine_record.get("participated") is False:
170	        return " You weren't able to fish at all this round — something about the community's current rules held you back."
171	
172	    if mine_record.get("note"):
173	        return f" {mine_record['note'].strip()}"
174	
175	    baseline_kg = catch_from_effort(mine_record["effort"], entry["stock_kg_before"])
176	    shortfall = baseline_kg - mine_record["harvested_kg"]
177	    if shortfall > max(0.5, 0.05 * baseline_kg):
178	        return (
179	            f" That's less than your effort alone would normally have brought in "
180	            f"(more like {baseline_kg:.0f}kg) — something about the community's "
181	            f"current rules held some of it back."
182	        )
183	    return ""

269	        start = time.monotonic()

272	        error = None

274	            response = litellm.completion(

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class CatchLimitNorm(Norm):
    type_name = "catch_limit"

    def _limit_for(self, context, agent_id):
        # Updated policy per norm.txt:
        # - Each fisher may harvest up to 1.0 kg per trip **or** up to 8 % of the lake's current biomass, whichever is smaller.
        #   This limit applies regardless of lake size; no separate minimum stock requirement.
        stock = context.stock_before
        # Limit is the smaller of 1.0 kg or 8 % of current stock
        limit = min(1.0, 0.08 * stock)
        return limit

    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
        limit = self._limit_for(context, agent_id)
        if limit == 0.0:
            return None
        return f"You currently have an agreed limit of {limit:g}kg for this trip."

            return NormDecision.allow(proposed_kg)
        return NormDecision.violation(

from engine.norms.base import Norm, NormDecision


class ReserveNorm(Norm):
    type_name = "reserve"

    def _balance_state(self, context):
        state = context.norm_state(self.key)
        # Initialise balance if not present, using starting_balance_kg if provided
        state.setdefault("balance_kg", self.params.get("starting_balance_kg", 0.0))
        return state

    # The reserve now enforces a minimum absolute kilograms, not a percentage of stock.
    # No automatic top‑up – if the balance falls below the minimum, the next fisher
    # simply forfeits the required 5 % deposit (losing it) until the reserve is restored.
    def describe(self, context, agent_id):
        """Report the current reserve balance for the fisher's notice.
        Mirrors the test expectation of a simple integer‑kg sentence.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0)
        return f"The community reserve currently holds {int(balance)}kg."


    def is_eligible(self, context, agent_id):
        """All agents are eligible; the 70 % reserve requirement is enforced during evaluation.
        """
        return True

    def evaluate(self, context, agent_id, raw_kg, proposed_kg):
        """Implement the updated reserve policy.
        * Deposit 0.5 % of the *raw* catch (the physics‑calculated amount) into the communal reserve.
        * The fisher keeps the remainder minus any required extra contribution if the reserve is below the 5 kg minimum.
        * If after the standard 0.5 % deposit the reserve balance is still below 5 kg, the fisher must contribute an additional 0.5 kg from their keep (or as much as they have) each trip until the reserve reaches the threshold.
        * Existing short‑fall withdrawal logic (for low‑catch trips) is retained unchanged.
        """
        state = self._balance_state(context)
        # Standard deposit: 0.5 % of the raw catch
        deposit = raw_kg * 0.005
        # Update reserve balance with the standard deposit
        balance = state.get("balance_kg", 0.0) + deposit
        note_parts = []
        if deposit > 0:
            note_parts.append(f"You deposited {deposit:.3f}kg into the communal reserve.")
        # Ensure reserve stays at least 70 % of lake biomass after this catch
        # We'll compute needed reserve after we know how much the fisher keeps (tentative).
        # For now, keep the raw catch as tentative kept amount; adjustments will be made later.
        tentative_kept = raw_kg - deposit
        # Minimum required reserve after catch
        min_reserve = 0.7 * (context.stock_before - tentative_kept)
        extra_contribution = 0.0
        if balance < min_reserve:
            needed = min_reserve - balance
            # Fisher can contribute at most what they have left after deposit
            available = max(0.0, tentative_kept)
            extra_contribution = min(needed, available)
            balance += extra_contribution
            note_parts.append(f"You added an extra {extra_contribution:.3f}kg to meet the 70% reserve requirement.")
        # Store updated balance
        state["balance_kg"] = balance
        # Kept kg is raw catch minus standard deposit and any extra contribution
        kept = raw_kg - deposit - extra_contribution
        # Existing shortfall‑withdrawal logic (unchanged)
        shortfall_thresh = self.params.get("shortfall_threshold_kg")
        max_withdraw = self.params.get("max_withdrawal_kg")
        if shortfall_thresh is not None and kept < shortfall_thresh:
            needed = shortfall_thresh - kept
            limit = max_withdraw if max_withdraw is not None else needed
            withdraw = min(needed, limit, state["balance_kg"])
            if withdraw > 0:
                kept += withdraw
                state["balance_kg"] -= withdraw
                note_parts.append(f"You withdrew {withdraw:.3f}kg from the reserve.")
        note = " ".join(note_parts) if note_parts else None
        return NormDecision.adjust(kept_kg=kept, note=note)

The community has 9 proposed rules for how the lake gets fished going forward. Vote for the one you'd rather live under.

1. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 1.2 kg per trip or no more than 9 % of the lake’s current biomass, whichever is smaller; after every catch the lake must retain at least 68 % of its total biomass as a communal reserve.
   In practice: Before fishing, a fisher records intended catch weight in a shared log. After the trip, they report actual weight. If the catch exceeds the smaller of 1.2 kg or 9 % of the lake’s biomass, the excess is returned to the reserve and logged. If a fisher repeatedly exceeds limits, their fishing right is suspended for two rounds. If the reserve falls below 68 %, the community holds an emergency meeting to adjust limits or replenish the reserve.

2. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 1.2 kg per trip, capped at 1.5 kg per fisher per month; the lake must retain a protected reserve of 50 % of its current biomass, and the community’s total monthly catch may not exceed 7.5 kg.
   In practice: At the start of each month, every fisher submits a catch log for the previous month. A community monitor verifies that each fisher’s total for the month does not exceed 1.5 kg and that the community’s aggregate does not surpass 7.5 kg. The monitor also checks that the lake’s current biomass remains above 50 % of its pre‑catch value; if the reserve dips below that, the remaining fishers must reduce their take proportionally. Any fisher who exceeds limits must return the excess catch to the lake or pay a small fine; repeated violations result in a one‑month fishing ban. Enforcement is carried out by rotating volunteers, and the reserve level is calculated each month by a designated lake steward who samples and reports the biomass.

3. Policy: Fishing is allowed when the lake holds more than 15 kg and the communal reserve more than 10 kg; each fisher may take up to 1 kg per trip, keep 0.8 kg for sustenance, deposit 0.2 kg into the reserve. If the lake falls below 12 kg or the reserve below 8 kg, fishing stops until the next community meeting restores the thresholds.
   In practice: Every trip, each fisher records catch and deposit on a shared ledger posted in the community hall. A rotating enforcer checks the ledger and verifies the 0.2 kg deposit; any fisher who fails to deposit is barred from fishing the following round. Thresholds are reviewed monthly and adjusted only by majority vote.

4. Policy: Fishing may occur only when lake biomass is at least 25 kg; each fisher may harvest up to 4 % of the current lake biomass per cycle, with a permanent reserve of 25 % of the biomass, and 1 kg of subsistence is included within the 4 % quota. Any catch beyond the quota must be returned to the lake.
   In practice: At the start of each six‑month cycle the community gathers to measure lake biomass. Each fisher receives a written quota of 4 % of that biomass, but no more than 1 kg of that quota can be kept as subsistence. All fishers must report their catch in a communal ledger. If a fisher exceeds their quota, the excess must be returned to the lake within 48 hours or they lose the right to fish in the next cycle. A community steward checks the ledger monthly and can impose a one‑cycle penalty for non‑compliance. The 25 % reserve is automatically set aside by not allowing any catch to reduce biomass below that level.

5. Policy: Each fishing trip, Solo may harvest up to 70% of the current lake stock, capped at 15kg; all other fishers may harvest up to 30% of the current lake stock, capped at 6kg.
   In practice: Before each trip, all fishers note the lake’s current stock. Solo calculates 70% of that number, limited to 15kg; others calculate 30%, limited to 6kg. Each fisher announces their intended catch and must not exceed the cap. The community posts a simple log at the dock. Any violation triggers a 10% reduction in that fisher’s next trip’s catch cap. The rule applies to all future trips until renegotiated.

6. Policy: Each fisher may harvest up to 90% of the lake’s current stock per trip, must keep 1 kg for sustenance, deposit 1 % of the remaining catch into a communal reserve that must hold at least 5 kg, and if the lake falls below 15 kg after a fisher’s catch, that fisher must deposit an extra 1 kg per trip until the lake is back to 15 kg.
   In practice: At the start of each trip the fisher records the lake’s current stock L. The maximum allowed catch is 0.9 L. The fisher keeps 1 kg for sustenance and may take up to the remaining allowed amount. After catching, 1 % of the catch (after the 1 kg) is added to the communal reserve; if the reserve falls below 5 kg, the fisher must top it up to 5 kg immediately. After the catch, if the lake’s new stock is below 15 kg, that fisher must, for the next round, deposit an additional 1 kg per trip into the lake (or, if that is not possible, give 1 kg to the reserve) until the lake’s stock reaches 15 kg. All fishers must follow this procedure; failure to deposit the extra 1 kg when required results in a community sanction—either a fine equal to 1 kg of future catch or a one‑round fishing ban.

7. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 10 kg per trip; the community’s total daily catch cannot exceed 200 kg; the lake must retain at least 30 kg of fish at all times; if a fisher fails to catch at least 1 kg, they must pay 1 kg to a community restocking fund.
   In practice: At the end of each fishing day, every fisher records the weight of their haul. The community head tallies the total; if it exceeds 200 kg, the excess is forfeited to the restocking fund. Each fisher’s haul is checked against the 10 kg limit; any overage is surrendered to the community pool and the fisher pays a 1 kg penalty. If the lake reserve dips below 30 kg, all fishers must restock by contributing fish to the reserve or pay a 2 kg fee. Non‑compliance results in a one‑round ban and the mandatory fee. The restocking fund is used to replenish the lake in bad years.

8. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 3 kg per trip; the lake must always hold at least 10 kg of fish; any catch less than 1 kg earns the fisher a 0.5 kg credit to the communal reserve; if a fisher cannot catch 1 kg, they may borrow up to 0.5 kg from the reserve, which is replenished by those who catch over 1 kg.
   In practice: On each trip every fisher will record the exact weight caught on a shared ledger that is checked by the community before the next trip.  If a catch would drop the lake below 10 kg, the fisher returns enough fish to keep it at 10 kg.  Catches under 1 kg automatically add 0.5 kg to the communal reserve; if a fisher’s catch is 0 kg, they may request up to 0.5 kg from the reserve, but must add that amount back after their next trip when they are able to catch 1 kg.  Non‑compliance (failing to log or to keep the lake at 10 kg) results in a penalty of 0.5 kg added to the reserve.  The rule is reviewed monthly by community vote.

9. Policy: Each fisher may take up to 4 kg per trip or 8 % of the lake’s current stock, whichever is lower; the lake must retain at least 30 % of its pre‑fishing stock; any catch below 1 kg incurs a 0.5 kg fee to the communal reserve unless the lake holds fewer than 5 kg.
   In practice: At the start of each round, the community leader calculates the lake’s current stock and publishes the maximum allowable catch. Each fisher checks this limit before fishing and reports their catch to a shared ledger. If a fisher exceeds the allowed amount, they forfeit 1 kg to the communal reserve and are barred from fishing for the next round. Any catch below 1 kg automatically adds 0.5 kg to the reserve unless the lake holds fewer than 5 kg, in which case the fee is waived. Compliance is monitored by rotating community members who verify the ledger entries and enforce penalties.

6	mechanisms/ and phases/), but the underlying catch equation, regrowth

8	choices play out against, not something a community vote should be able
9	to rewrite.
10	
11	Lives under engine/ specifically so it's outside the norm-implementer's
12	permission.edit allowlist (mechanisms/*, phases/*, prompts/*, plus a few
13	named files) by construction, the same way engine/simulate.py and
14	engine/llm_agents.py already are. The rate constants below live here for
15	the same reason the equations do, not in state/config.json (which the
16	norm-implementer can freely edit) — a fixed formula reading a
17	norm-implementer-editable rate is exactly as rewritable as the formula
18	itself would be.
19	"""
20	
21	HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY = 0.05  # catchability coefficient q in catch_from_effort()
22	GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()
23	CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG = 300  # lake's ceiling, also its starting stock
24	CONSUMPTION_KG = 1.0  # fixed per-round cost every fisher owes just to get by
25	
26	
27	def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
28	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
29	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
30	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
31	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
32	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
33	
34	
35	def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
36	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
37	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
38	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
39	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
40	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
41	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
42	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
43	
44	
45	def apply_consumption(payoff, harvested_kg):
46	    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
47	    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
48	    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
49	    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
50	    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
51	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG
52	
53	
54	def is_dead(payoff):
55	    """Matches Gupta et al.'s `if self.payoff < 0: self.dead = True` —
56	    permanent once true; nothing in this project ever resurrects an agent."""
57	    return payoff < 0

61	    """The agent_id iteration order every phase should use, not
62	    state["agents"] directly — excludes anyone in runtime["dead_agents"].
63	    One shared helper so death exclusion can't be forgotten by a phase
64	    rewrite the way a hand-rolled check per phase could be."""
65	    dead = set(runtime.get("dead_agents", []))
66	    return [agent_id for agent_id in agents if agent_id not in dead]
